messages.subject: wrong mean curve using stat_sum_single()
parts:
Hello users,

I recently find some discrepancy between the mean value using stat_sum_single() in ggplot2 and mean calculate using aggregate (..... ,mean) function. The code is as follows. Black line is the mean calculated using stat_sum_single() in ggplot2. Red line is the mean from aggregate function. I am using ggplot2 0.9.1 and R 2.15.1. Can anyone provide some explanations? Many thanks!!!

stat_sum_single <- function(fun, geom="point", ...) {
  stat_summary(fun.y=fun, geom=geom,...)
}

ggplot(subset(pkData3,DOSE==20),aes(TIME,DV))+
  geom_point(aes(TIME,DV),colour="blue",size=3,shape=1)+
  stat_sum_single(mean, geom="line",colour="black",size=1.2)+
  geom_line(aes(TIME,DV,group=ID),colour="blue")+
  geom_line(aes(TIME,mean),colour="red",size=1)+
  facet_wrap(~DOSE,scales = "fix")+
   xlab("Time (h)")+
  scale_y_log10(breaks=c(0.1,1,10,100))

messages.subject: Re: wrong mean curve using stat_sum_single()
parts:
Hi:

Without a reproducible example, there's no way to tell the difference, but I'm wondering if perhaps you have some missing data and one function accounts for it in computing the mean while the other doesn't (in terms of effective sample size)??? Pure speculation...a reproducible example would provide a way to test that and/or other hypotheses.

Dennis
